definition: Ernie Bot (Chinese: 文心一言, Pinyin: wénxīn yīyán), full name Enhanced Representation through Knowledge Integration, is an artificial intelligence chatbot developed by the Chinese technology company Baidu.
details: Ernie Bot rivals GPT models in Chinese NLP tasks. It is built on the company's ERNIE series of large language models, which have been in development since 2019. The service was first launched for invited testing on March 16, 2023, and was released to the general public on August 31, 2023, after receiving approval from Chinese regulators. Since its public launch, Ernie Bot has undergone several updates, with newer versions like ERNIE 4.0 and 4.5 released to improve its capabilities. The service has seen rapid user adoption, reportedly reaching over 200 million users by April 2024. It has been integrated into various products, notably powering AI features for the Chinese release of Samsung's Galaxy S24 smartphones. As a product operating in China, Ernie Bot is subject to the country's censorship regulations. It has been observed to refuse answers to politically sensitive questions, such as those regarding CCP general secretary Xi Jinping, the 1989 Tiananmen Square protests and massacre, and other topics deemed taboo by the government.

explainer.lead: Ernie Bot is Baidu's AI chatbot, built on the company's ERNIE large language models developed since 2019. It matters as a Chinese alternative to GPT-style models, particularly for Chinese-language NLP tasks.

tiers.eli5: It's a chatbot you can talk to in Chinese, made by a big Chinese tech company, kind of like having a conversation with a very well-read assistant.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers use it as a hosted conversational model for Chinese-language tasks. A pitfall is the regulatory gating: it was invite-only from March 2023 and only reached the public in August 2023 after Chinese regulator approval, so access and deployment can be constrained.
tiers.paperLevel: Ernie Bot is a chatbot service built on the ERNIE series of large language models; it has no single formal definition. Limits are practical: availability began restricted to invited testing on March 16, 2023, and public access depended on regulator approval.

explainer.example: A developer building a Chinese-language support bot calls Ernie Bot rather than a GPT model, and later upgrades to ERNIE 4.0 or 4.5 to improve capability.
